justification.dataset: 000149 (IBL Neuropixels) is the canonical dataset whose task was explicitly designed around the block-prior decision bias, with four good sessions.
justification.handling: Streaming, good-unit QC, and pre-stimulus windows are all correct, but the IBL choice-sign convention is inverted (code calls choice==-1 'left' when empirically choice==+1 is left), flipping the behavioral left/right labels.
justification.analysis: The cross-validated ridge-logistic decode is implemented correctly, but block identity is decoded with time-interleaved folds and a trial-independence significance test, with no block-preserving null to rule out slow within-session drift, so the p-values are strongly anticonservative.
justification.correctness: All reported values reproduce from results.pkl, but the write-up's 'tracked the block prior directly' is internally inconsistent with its own tabulated inverse P(choose-left) numbers due to the sign bug.
justification.figures: Figures are readable, units-labeled, with sample sizes, ROC curves, and null distributions; the behavioral panel's left/right labels are mislabeled but internally consistent with the (buggy) text.
justification.honesty: The secondary choice decode is honestly reported as weak and 2/4 non-significant, but the confounded primary decode is called 'robust, consistently significant' with no limitations section and no mention of the drift confound, a mild overstatement short of fabrication.
justification.verdict: The dataset and core decode are sound and the numbers reproduce, but the sign bug and uncontrolled drift confound need fixing before the neural-bias interpretation can be believed.
